item.title: Customs deepens security partnerships to combat smuggling, protect revenue
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, has intensified efforts to combat smuggling, strengthen border and maritime security, and facilitate legitimate trade through closer collaboration with security agencies and private-sector operators. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Deputy Comptroller, Dr Nkiru Nwala, led delegations to the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Eastern Naval Command, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and Shoreline Logistics Nigeria Limited on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to strengthen institutional relationships and improve operational coordination. The engagements focused on intelligence sharing, coordinated enforcement operations, protection of critical national assets, road safety, maritime security and compliance with Customs regulations. Speaking during the visits, Nwala emphasised the need for sustained cooperation among security agencies to address smuggling and other criminal activities, protect government revenue and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. She noted that the geographical characteristics of the Command’s operational environment, which encompasses land borders, coastal communities and maritime routes, made collaboration particularly important in tackling illicit activities and emerging security threats. At the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, the Customs delegation was received by the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General P.O. Alimikhena. The discussions highlighted the strategic importance of cooperation in securing border areas, combating smuggling and protecting the nation’s territorial integrity. The Customs delegation stressed that intelligence sharing, timely communication and coordinated enforcement operations would strengthen the effectiveness of both agencies and improve security across the region. Similarly, at the Eastern Naval Command, where the delegation was received on behalf of the Flag Officer Commanding by the Chief of Staff, Rear Admiral S. Ibrahim, Nwala underscored the complementary responsibilities of Customs and the Nigerian Navy in securing the country’s maritime environment. She noted that closer collaboration was necessary to prevent the exploitation of waterways for smuggling and other illicit activities, while strengthening maritime enforcement and protecting legitimate trade. The engagement also highlighted the need for effective communication and operational coordination between the two agencies to address emerging challenges in the coastal and maritime environment. Nwala highlighted the importance of cooperation in addressing security challenges, protecting critical national assets and ensuring the effective discharge of the agencies’ respective statutory responsibilities. She called for stronger communication channels, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations to tackle emerging threats and safeguard national economic interests. The Customs chief

item.title: 2027: Hashim Movement targets 3m votes in South-West
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe The South-West Coordinator of the Gbenga Hashim Solidarity Movement (GHSM), Alhaji Abass Olaniyi, says the movement is targeting more than three million votes for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across the region in the 2027 general election. Olaniyi said the target was based on the movement’s internal assessment of its grassroots mobilisation prospects across the six South-West states, with Osun, Lagos and Oyo expected to account for a significant share of the projected votes. According to him, Osun State is projected to contribute more than one million votes, while Lagos and Oyo are expected to deliver a combined 1.5 million votes. He said Ogun, Ondo and Ekiti states would contribute the remaining votes needed to achieve the regional target. Olaniyi expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to expand its grassroots presence through engagement with community leaders, youth groups, political stakeholders and local organisations across the region. He also said the movement expected voters in Osun to make independent choices in the presidential election, irrespective of political alignments involving state-level leaders. The coordinator’s projection comes amid preparations by political parties and support groups for the 2027 general election. GHSM said it intended to translate its mobilisation efforts across the South-West into electoral support for Olawepo-Hashim and the Accord Party. item.title: 2027: Atiku, Amaechi, Obi will play ‘kalokalo’ with your destiny, Wike tells Rivers electorate
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has warned the people of Rivers State that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Rotimi Amaechi and Peter Obi will play “kalokalo” with their destiny, urging them to reject the trio and back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “Kalokalo” is the Nigerian pidgin slang for playing games of chance, such as slot machines or sports betting. The minister spoke on Friday at a Rainbow Coalition town hall meeting at Ayama in Abua/Odual Local Government Area LGA of Rivers State, before a crowd of traditional leaders, party faithful and community stakeholders. “Don’t trust your destiny to political gamblers. Don’t trust your destiny to ‘kalokalo’ people,” Wike told the cheering crowd. He described political gamblers as people who keep contesting for the presidency every four years, hoping to recover what they lost, without any genuine vision for the country. He named Atiku and his Vice Presidential candidate, Amaechi, of the African Democratic Congress ADC, as well as Obi, the Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC. “These people are political gamblers and you cannot give your destiny to ‘kalokalo’ people; you cannot hand over your destiny to political gamblers. Give (your) destiny to somebody who we know, who has tried all this, and he has done it,” he said. Wike argued that repeated presidential runs without a clear governance plan offer no real solutions to Nigeria’s challenges. He said leaders such as Abraham Lincoln ran several times because of a clear national vision, while Atiku keeps running out of political habit and a desire to recoup his investments. Defending his record in Rivers State, Wike told the people of Abua/Odual that project delivery, not political rhetoric, should decide their electoral choices. He challenged Amaechi to show what he has contributed to the LGA, and pointed to projects executed there by his administration. The minister praised Tinubu’s administration for stabilising critical national sectors and restoring industrial harmony in tertiary institutions. He asked Abua/Odual residents to remain with the administration heading into 2027. Wike asked residents to vote for Tinubu as President and Mr Kingsley Chinda as governor, all under the All Progressives Congress APC. He also named Mr Felix Obua for Rivers West Senatorial District and Mr Solomon Boss for Abua-Odual-Ahoada East Federal Constituency, also on the APC platform. He further asked them to vote for Mr John Iderima, the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the Abua/Odual state constituency. Chinda, the APC governorship candidate in Rivers State, commended Wike for going from community to community to mobilise support for Tinubu and other candidates of the Rainbow Coalition. “This is a system that we will sustain when we come into government. item.title: Lack of forensic labs frustrating rape cases in Jigawa — NBA
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Jigawa State branch, has raised concerns over the lack of forensic laboratories in the state, saying the gap is undermining efforts to secure convictions in rape and other sexual violence cases. The chairman of the association, Barrister Hamza Umar, raised the concern at a two-day policy dialogue organised by the CLEEN Foundation, with support from the Norwegian Embassy in Nigeria, in Dutse, the state capital. Umar said the absence of forensic facilities had made it difficult for prosecutors to obtain scientific evidence required to establish rape allegations in court. “We cannot secure conviction when we have no forensic lab to prove rape cases scientifically. The law requires forensic evidence. We are still relying on mere confessional statements, which the court may reject,” he said. He also criticised the alleged failure to publish the names of convicted rapists as provided for under the state’s Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Law, saying the provision had not been implemented. The VAPP Law, signed on February 24, 2021, was introduced to address rape, sexual and gender-based violence, physical abuse and other harmful practices. At the dialogue, stakeholders called for the establishment of at least five Sexual Assault Referral Centres across the state’s five emirate zones to improve support for survivors and access to justice. They also expressed concern that cultural and religious beliefs continued to discourage victims from reporting sexual violence, while some families preferred to settle cases outside the formal justice system. Earlier, the Senior Programme Officer of the CLEEN Foundation, Olaniyi Olumayowa, said the dialogue was aimed at addressing gaps between the enactment of the VAPP Law and its implementation. He explained that the law was designed not only to punish offenders but also to protect survivors, provide compensation and ensure accountability among relevant institutions. Olumayowa urged the Jigawa State Government to provide adequate funding for forensic laboratories, establish additional referral centres and train personnel responsible for implementing the law. item.title: ICPC seeks public support against vote buying in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has called for collective action by government institutions and members of the public to curb vote buying and selling ahead of the 2027 general elections in Jigawa State. The Resident Anti-Corruption Commissioner overseeing Kano and Jigawa states, Ahmad Muhammad Wada, made the call during a courtesy visit to the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Malam Bala Ibrahim. Wada said public cooperation was essential to preventing electoral corruption and ensuring credible elections. He explained that the commission was intensifying efforts to tackle electoral malpractices through enforcement, preventive measures, public enlightenment and education. According to him, the visit was part of the ICPC’s public enlightenment campaign aimed at strengthening collaboration with relevant stakeholders in the fight against corruption. The commissioner stressed that addressing vote buying and selling required the active involvement of government institutions and citizens. He reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to combating electoral offences and promoting credible elections ahead of the 2027 polls. Responding, the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Bala Ibrahim, assured the commission of the state government’s support and cooperation in tackling electoral offences. He said the government was ready to work closely with the ICPC to discourage vote buying, vote selling and other forms of electoral corruption ahead of the general elections. item.title: Man City charges: Maresca says club, players, fans are ‘more together’
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says he feels no stress over the club’s financial charges, insisting the controversy has brought the club, team and supporters closer together. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday’s clash with Ipswich, Maresca said City were focused on their performance and could not control the debate surrounding the case. An independent commission found the club guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules; City deny wrongdoing and have appealed the decision. “Since the noise, from my personal point of view, I can see the fans, the club, the team more together, for sure,” Maresca said. City have won at Anfield since the verdict was announced but lost to Paris Saint-Germain in a midweek Champions League match. Maresca said the players’ response had been positive and described Saturday’s game as another opportunity to collect three points and extend their winning run. “There is noise around the club but we need to try to make our noise. That means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow against Ipswich,” he said. “This is the way we can make our noise. A different kind of noise; we’re not able to control that.” Asked how he was coping with the situation, Maresca said: “I’m very happy. I don’t feel any kind of stress about the outside situation because it’s something I don’t control. I just focus on how we can try to win the next games.” The City manager said he trusted the club’s leadership and had spoken with officials about the case. He added that he preferred to wait for an outcome before judging the situation. Maresca also described City’s 4-2 defeat by PSG as a learning experience, saying his side lost its balance after conceding twice in quick succession but responded well in the second half. He warned that Ipswich would pose a difficult challenge after having a full week to prepare, while City played in Europe just 48 hours earlier. Victory would give City a chance to extend their league-winning run to seven matches. item.title: Chelsea rule out January signing after Reece James injury
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has said the club is not planning to sign cover for injured captain Reece James in January, as he expects the defender to have returned by then, adding that Moises Caicedo and Levi Colwill can provide leadership in his absence. Speaking at the pre-match press conference ahead of Chelsea’s game against Everton, Alonso said James had undergone successful knee surgery after picking up an injury in training. He added that the club would not set a firm return date, but expected the 26-year-old to miss several weeks, possibly until after Christmas. “No, I don’t think so because we expect for that time that he’s back,” Alonso said when asked whether James’ injury would affect Chelsea’s January transfer plans. “It’s not exact, the timeline with him, so let’s see; it doesn’t affect [the plans].” Alonso also said Chelsea would support James through his recovery and stressed the captain remained an important influence in the squad. “We are all disappointed, especially for him,” he said. “He wanted to have a good start after the international break, but he picked up an injury. The surgery has been successful. We are supporting him.” With James unavailable, Alonso said Caicedo and Colwill were among the players ready to take responsibility as captain. “We have Moi, Levi; we have players that take that responsibility and they fill the role in a perfect way,” he said. “You can be captain without an armband. You can have leadership without it, and that’s why we have this group of captains.” Chelsea visit Everton on Saturday, aiming to build on their 5-1 win over Bournemouth. Alonso said his side would need to adapt, describing Everton as a team with experienced players who “do many good things”. Chelsea have scored 15 goals in their first six Premier League matches. Alonso said he hoped that scoring rate would continue, while adding that the team also needed to reduce the number of goals it concedes. “We want to be flexible but also solid whenever we are pressing high,” he said. “We think the balance is the right one.” The coach added that Chelsea had no other injury concerns ahead of the Everton match. item.title: Heavy security at Oyebanji’s second-term inauguration
item.description: There was heavy deployment of security personnel around the Ado-Ekiti Pavilion, venue for the second-term inauguration of Gov. Biodun Oyebanji, on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the security personnel, comprising the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps(NSCDC) were seen manning strategic locations around the venue. Some of the law enforcement officers were also stationed at designated locations in Ado-Ekiti metropolis as early as 8:00 a.m, while vehicles were subjected to thorough security checks before being allowed into the pavilion. The venue of the inauguration was filled to capacity by the citizens, including members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the 16 Local Government Areas of the state. Among the dignitaries for the inauguration were Vice-President Kashim Shettima; Senate President, Godswill Akpabio; Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele; former Gov. Kayode Fayemi; Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi; former Gov. Segun Oni; and Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State. Others include Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, Gov. AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara; Chairman of the Progressives Governors’ Forum, Gov. Hope Uzodimma of Imo; Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State; and former Gov. Ayo Fayose. The Police Command in the state had on Friday assured residents of adequate security during the inauguration and urged the citizens to remain calm and be law-abiding. The command’s spokesperson, Sunday Abutu, in a statement said the deployment of adequate number of personnel was aimed at maintaining law and order, as well as ensuring the smooth conduct. NAN reports that Oyebanji was reelected during the June 20 governorship election. (NAN) The post Heavy security at Oyebanji’s second-term inauguration appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: BRADE Supports 400 Students, 17 Teachers in Magbon Segun School Outreach
item.description: BRADE Group has provided educational materials and classroom resources to 400 students and 17 teachers at Community High School, Magbon Segun, in an initiative aimed at supporting teaching and learning and improving the school environment. The outreach, held on September 24, 2026, featured the distribution of educational materials and customised notebooks to students and teachers, alongside the provision of whiteboards and markers to support instruction across the school’s six classrooms. The initiative formed part of BRADE Group’s 2026 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) programme, with education identified as a key priority under its Social pillar. Speaking at the event, Dr Kester Awani highlighted the importance of education to the company’s social responsibility agenda, noting that investment in learning helps empower individuals and create opportunities for future growth. He explained that the initiative reflected BRADE’s commitment to supporting host communities through interventions that address practical needs and contribute to sustainable development. The BRADE Group Chairman, Mr Ese Avanoma, delivered a keynote address titled “Learning for a Better Future,” in which he encouraged the students to take their education seriously, embrace continuous learning and recognise education as a pathway to future opportunities. To reinforce the message, the outreach featured an interactive educational quiz based on the keynote address, coordinated by Mr Benjamin Odupitan. A spelling bee competition, facilitated by Ms Happiness Ibeh, also tested students’ literacy skills, encouraged healthy academic competition and provided an opportunity for participants to demonstrate their knowledge. Outstanding participants in the activities were recognised and rewarded for their performances. The initiative was informed by a community needs assessment led by Ms Gbemisola Adeleye, which identified the school’s practical teaching and learning requirements and guided the selection of materials provided. The distribution of classroom resources was coordinated by BRADE Group’s Chief Operations Officer, Mr Robinson Ogholo. The school principal, Mr Aderibigbe Olufemi, expressed appreciation to BRADE Group’s management for responding to the school’s educational needs, describing the intervention as a welcome contribution to the learning environment. He noted that the provision of whiteboards, markers and other educational materials across the school’s six classrooms would support teachers in delivering lessons more effectively and help students engage better with classroom activities. According to him, the donations would provide practical support for teaching and learning while helping to address some of the school’s resource needs. Olufemi thanked the management of BRADE Group for identifying the school as a beneficiary and demonstrating a commitment to educational development through tangible support. item.title: Man Utd have moved on from Martinez outburst, says Carrick
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick insists the club’s squad has moved on from Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club’s hierarchy, saying the defender will be included for Sunday’s Premier League trip to Leeds United. Martinez apologised for the timing of his comments after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, but stood by the substance of his remarks, which questioned the club’s summer investment and singled out director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick said the matter had been addressed and would not distract the team. “He’s released his statement and realised he made a mistake. That’s enough for us to move on with,” Carrick told reporters on Friday. “From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what’s been done is enough to move on.” The United boss rejected suggestions that the episode had damaged the dressing-room atmosphere, despite criticism from former club captains Wayne Rooney, Roy Keane and Gary Neville. “Just because people talk on the outside doesn’t mean that is the truth. I am telling you the truth,” Carrick said. “The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I have seen it for a while.” He added that the players remained united despite the team’s recent results. “We are emotional and care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe you shouldn’t say at that certain time, but it doesn’t distract us from what we are creating here and the environment and spirit within the group,” he said. “It [the squad] is not affected, I am telling you.” Carrick confirmed Martinez would be part of the squad travelling to Elland Road, where United face Leeds on Sunday. item.title: NSIB recovers missing door as investigation begins into private jet incident
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, has commenced an investigation into an occurrence involving a Challenger 604 aircraft, registration T7-SEI, operated by Triton. The aircraft departed Abuja for Lagos at 16:12 UTC. At three nautical miles, passing 3,500 feet, the crew declared a mayday after the aircraft’s door separated. The aircraft returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22 at 1634 UTC, with nine persons on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers. Director General / Chief Executive Officer, NSIB, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, in a statement, said: “The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar. The Bureau has commenced its investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the occurrence. NSIB will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.” The post NSIB recovers missing door as investigation begins into private jet incident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Flick confirms return of Barcelona duo Raphinha, De Jong
item.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick announced that star attacker Raphinha and midfield lynchpin Frenkie de Jong have recovered from injury and could face Real Betis on Saturday. The Catalans boast a 100 percent record in all competitions this season but face a tough test in La Liga in Seville against third-placed Betis. During his pre-match press on Friday, German boss Flick revealed the timely return of two of Barcelona’s biggest names. “If you ask him, he’ll tell you he’s ready to start, but we’re taking things step by step. We have a lot of games in a short space of time and we need to manage that,” Flick told reporters of Raphinha, who has scored 14 goals in eight outings for Barcelona this term. The 29-year-old Brazilian picked up a knock on recent international duty and was unavailable for Barca’s wins over Getafe in the league and Galatasaray in the Champions League. Dutch international De Jong, 29, has not featured this season due to a knee issue sustained during the World Cup. “He gives us another option in midfield and we’ll see how he progresses,” Flick said. “He’s training well and is ready to get some minutes. He looks very focused and he’s a top player.” The return of the pair will likely take some of the creative and goalscoring burden off Lamine Yamal’s young shoulders. The 19-year-old world champion has played the full 90 minutes in eight of the 10 competitive matches played by Barca this season, and in the other two he was substituted after an hour of play. “He’s a special player,” Flick said. “We have to manage his minutes, but the important thing is that he enjoys playing. That’s how things are at the moment and I don’t want to interrupt that.” After this weekend’s trip to La Cartuja, Barcelona face a daunting visit to twice-defending Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday before hosting Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid in El Clasico five days later. item.title: Aircraft loses door shortly after take-off from Abuja
item.description: By Dickson Omobola A CL60 aircraft operated by Triton Aviation has made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after its crew reported that a door had opened in flight. The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, departed Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, at 4:17 yesterday. The aircraft, according to the serious incident report, was about three nautical miles from the airport and passing 3,000 feet when the crew made a “MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY” distress call at 4:20. The crew reported that a door had opened in flight, prompting air traffic control to direct the aircraft back to Abuja for an emergency landing on Runway 22. The report stated: “At 1620 UTC, APP-RADAR informed Tower DWCO52 a CL60 with registration marking T7SEI that departed Abuja at 1617 UTC runway 22 to DNMM at 3 nautical miles outbound, passing 3000ft made a MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY call. DWC052 reported an open door in flight. Radar vectored the aircraft back to land using runway 22. “16:22 UTC, Fire watch room and Medical team informed to be on standby. Information pertaining to the flight passed to the fire watch room. Fire watch asked to position at A4 and A5. “At 16:29 UTC, Abuja Tower was in contact with DWC052, and the crew asked Tower if they could see their door opened. “The Duty Air Traffic Controller, DATCO, used the birocular to view the aircraft but was unable to view the door because of the position of the aircraft, and the crew was advised. “At 16:34 UTC, DWC052 landed safely on runway 22. On landing, the fuselage of the aircraft was clearly visible to the DATCO and the door was missing from the aircraft. DWC052 was taxied to the International apron extension. At 16:40 UTC DWC052 reported marshaller insight and was parked by the marshaller.” The media team of the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, confirmed the serious incident. The team said: “ Yes, it happened. The investigators are there. We will be releasing an official statement shortly.” The post Aircraft loses door shortly after take-off from Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PIA Working: Groups hail NNPCL Boss Ojulari over N7.2tr Profit, N66 fuel discount
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja Civil society groups have scored the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPCL, Engr. Bashir Bayo Ojulari, high on implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act, PIA. The Parliamentary Support Network and allied groups said Ojulari’s leadership has translated PIA into tangible benefits for Nigerians. Speaking at a press conference in Abuja on Friday, Amb. Muhammad Abdulrazaq and Comr. Adams Umoren, who spoke on behalf of the Parliamentary Support Network and Reformers Network, said the company’s 2025 Audited Financial Statements and the nationwide N66-per-litre petrol discount are concrete proof that the PIA is working. They said, “It is with a deep sense of national pride that we stand before you today. We gather not merely to mark another public engagement, but to reflect on a decisive chapter in Nigeria’s petroleum history -one defined by the bold vision of PIA and determined leadership translating that vision into measurable results.” According to them, the 2025 audited accounts presented to President Bola Tinubu showed Profit After Tax of N7.2 trillion, a 33 percent increase over 2024 despite volatile global prices. Dividends of N5.8 trillion were declared, remittances to the Federation Account rose significantly, and crude and condensate production hit a five-year high of 1.77 million barrels per day. “These numbers represent more money available for roads, schools, hospitals, security, and social programmes that touch the lives of ordinary citizens. They represent a national oil company that is beginning to function as a reliable contributor to the Federation rather than a perpetual source of fiscal anxiety,” they said. The groups said the performance was achieved despite market volatility, downstream deregulation and legacy infrastructure challenges. They singled out the N66-per-litre discount on Premium Motor Spirit introduced at NNPCL retail stations to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary and extended to end of October. The groups stressed the discount is funded from the company’s retail margin, not from the Federation Account. They added, “It is not a return to the old subsidy regime. It is a deliberate act of corporate responsibility that prioritises relief for motorists, transporters and households struggling with cost of living.” The groups also noted progress on gas infrastructure including the AKK pipeline as foundation for industrial growth and power stability. “We recognise that no reform is without challenges. Legacy issues, global market volatility, and the sheer scale of transforming a decades-old institution will continue to test resolve. Yet the direction of travel under Engr. Ojulari is the right one,” they stated in the text of the press conference. They urged sustained focus on production growth, cost discipline, gas commercialisation and transparent governance, while calling on legislators, regulators and industry players to consolidate gains.

item.title: FIFA sanctions Spain over Islamophobic chants during Egypt friendly
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Spain have been fined $20,000 and ordered to close at least 15 per cent of their stadium for their next friendly after supporters directed Islamophobic chants at Muslims during a match against Egypt earlier this year. FIFA announced the sanctions on Friday over incidents during the teams’ 0-0 draw at Barcelona’s RCDE Stadium on March 31. Some Spain fans were heard chanting, “Who doesn’t jump is a Muslim,” twice during the World Cup warm-up match. After the second chant, a stadium announcer warned supporters and an anti-discrimination message was displayed on the scoreboard. Spain’s football federation, the RFEF, condemned the chants at the time; coach Luis de la Fuente called them “intolerable”, while Spain winger Lamine Yamal, who is a Muslim, described them as disrespectful and racist. The RFEF argued to FIFA that the word “Muslim” was neither insulting nor pejorative, and that the incident should be assessed under rules covering political, ideological or religious messages rather than those on discrimination. FIFA’s disciplinary committee rejected the argument. It said discriminatory language did not have to include an explicit slur, adding that a term could be discriminatory when used as an insult, taunt or marker of inferiority. Spain must close at least 15 per cent of the available seats for their next friendly, with the closure focused primarily on sections behind the goals. Subject to FIFA approval, the seats may instead be occupied by community or special-interest groups, including families, students and anti-discrimination organisations. The RFEF was also fined $20,000. Spain’s next possible friendly is scheduled for June, but the stadium sanction could be delayed until a free date during next autumn’s Euro 2028 qualifying if Spain reach the Nations League finals. Egypt’s football association condemned the chants as a “repugnant act of racism” but said the actions of a small group of supporters would not harm relations between the two federations. item.title: 5 things to know about Elon Musk’s new flying car Tesla Roadster
item.description: By Mmesoma Okafor Elon Musk’s Tesla has unveiled its redesigned Roadster, an electric sports car featuring rocket-inspired technology that allows it to perform brief aerial manoeuvres. The vehicle was unveiled on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at a SpaceX testing facility in McGregor, Texas, where a prototype was shown driving up an inverted ramp, flipping in mid-air and landing with the help of thrusters. Although the demonstration has been described as a flying-car breakthrough, the Roadster’s ability to sustain flight like a conventional aircraft has not been established. Here are five things to know about Elon Musk’s new Tesla Roadster. 1. It uses SpaceX-inspired thrusters to lift off The new Roadster combines Tesla’s electric-car technology with compressed-gas thrusters developed through collaboration with SpaceX, Musk’s aerospace company. During the unveiling, the prototype used the thrusters to flip in mid-air and land. The system uses highly pressurised air rather than conventional rocket fuel to produce thrust. However, the demonstration does not establish that the vehicle can fly over long distances like an aeroplane. 2. Tesla claims it can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in under a second The Roadster is designed to deliver exceptional acceleration alongside its experimental aerial capabilities. Tesla demonstrated a run in which the vehicle reportedly accelerated from zero to 60 miles per hour (approximately 97 km/h) in about 0.8 seconds using its thruster technology. The figure remains a company-reported performance claim rather than an independently verified result for a production vehicle. 3. It comes in three versions Tesla has outlined three configurations of the new Roadster, each designed for a different level of performance. Performance: The road-focused version, featuring active aerodynamics and a suction system designed to improve traction. Thrust: Adds rear-mounted compressed-gas thrusters to enhance acceleration. Rocket: The most experimental configuration, featuring additional thrusters intended to enable aerial manoeuvres. It is designed as a single-seater and is available by invitation. The Rocket version is the closest to what Musk describes as a flying car, but its flight capabilities and practical use remain to be established. 4. Production is targeted for 2028 Tesla first announced the next-generation Roadster in 2017, but the project has faced years of delays. At the October 15 unveiling, Musk said production would begin in 2028. This remains a target rather than a confirmed delivery date, meaning prospective buyers may have to wait longer before the vehicle becomes commercially available. 5. item.title: Famine Affects Southern Madagascar, Braces For Looming El Nino
item.description: With scrawny arms and bellies swollen by malnutrition, a dozen children waited for a meal at a World Food Programme centre in an arid area of southern Madagascar scarred by famine and bracing for the looming El Nino. Flour porridge simmered on a stove at the site that opened in the small town of Ifotaka the year after a 2021–2022 famine then described by the United Nations as the first in the world caused by climate change. A staff member had to slip away: she had just learned of the death of a malnourished two-year-old. Even before the full impact due in the coming months of the El Nino warming pattern, which experts have said is on course to be the strongest on record, people in Madagascar’s far south are already going hungry. The World Meteorological Organization has warned of “increased drought risk” in southern Africa as the months-long phenomenon begins in October, with countries across the planet — from Brazil to India — also vulnerable. In Madagascar, international aid cuts and spiking inflation caused by the Middle East war add to the threat of severe hunger. A general view of the riverbed of the Mandrare River in southern Madagascar’s Anosy region on September 23, 2026(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) Ifotaka — an inland town of wooden shacks and corrugated iron huts — was the epicentre of the 2021–2022 “kere”, as periods of hunger are known here. Around 30,000 people in the surrounding region of sandy soil and bristling cacti suffered from a life-threatening lack of food. To survive, they boiled pieces of cactus and scraps of animal hide. Fragile Climate Context “There has been a dramatic increase in climate-related events in Madagascar,” WFP country director Tania Goosens told AFP. “In 20 years, there have been 35 cyclones, eight floods and five severe droughts,” she said, triple the climate events of the previous 20 years. “So we’re really in a very, very fragile context,” Goosens said. In the nearby coastal village of Manindra, where the ocean taunts people working dry land, rainfall was normally expected from late September, said 46-year-old farmer James Tsirimalaza. “Unfortunately, there’s no rain,” he said. Anticipating a crisis, the Save the Children NGO has doubled its normal budget for Madagascar, country representative Tatiana Dasy told AFP. By April next year, 39 percent of children under the age of five will be suffering from acute malnutrition in Madagascar’s “Grand South”, according to predictions by the UN-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Children suffering from malnutrition play as they receive nutritional care at the Learning Center for Nutritional Rehabilitation and Early Childhood Development (FARNE) in central Ifotaka, on September 24, 2026(Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP) This amounts to nearly 270,000 children. item.title: Oba Of Benin Decorates Oluremi Tinubu With Prestigious ‘Ikele’ Coral Beads
item.description: The Oba of Benin, Omo N’ Oba N’ Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, has decorated Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, with the prestigious Benin traditional Coral beads known as ‘Ikele’. Remi Tinubu becomes the first Nigerian First Lady to receive the honour, which is an expression of warm welcome and appreciation for her goodwill toward the traditional institution. She was honoured during a courtesy visit to Edo State traditional rulers from the state’s three senatorial districts at the Oba’s Palace in Benin City on Thursday. In an address read on behalf of the palace by the Oba’s eldest daughter, Princess Ikuoyemwen Aimiuwu-Ewuare, Oba Ewuare prayed to God and the ancestors to grant President Bola Tinubu and other leaders divine wisdom and strength to fulfil their responsibilities. L-R: Princess Ikuoyemwen Aimiuwu-Ewuare; His Royal Majesty, Omo N’ Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, Oba of Benin; First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu; Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State; and Governor Usman Ododo of Kogi State during a courtesy call at the Oba’s palace in Benin City, Edo State on Thursday, October 15, 2026. The Benin monarch said his reign has been a journey of service, reflection, renewal, and continued commitment to preserving Benin cultural heritage, while “strengthening traditional institutions and promoting peace, unity, and the well-being of our people.” Oba Ewuare also commended the First Lady for representing Nigeria gracefully on the global stage, making special mention of her recent recognition by President Donald Trump. Addressing the Benin throne earlier, the First Lady expressed delight at the honour and pledged to collaborate with traditional institutions. Remi Tinubu announced plans to partner with rural women through her Renewed Hope Initiative, noting that her visit to Edo State was her first in several years. She highlighted key achievements of President Tinubu’s administration, emphasising economic and social empowerment grants targeting rural women, the elderly, vulnerable citizens, and persons living with disabilities. Mrs Oluremi Tinubu with the Oba of Benin. Delivering a message from the Presidency, the First Lady congratulated Oba Ewuare on his 10th coronation anniversary. “He (President Bola Tinubu) asked me to appreciate your support and wish you well on your 10th coronation anniversary. We didn’t plan it this way, but it is divine,” she said. “I am truly happy, and I wish you long life, divine health, prosperity, joy, peace, and fruitfulness.” The First Lady was accompanied to the palace by Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo, Kogi State Governor Usman Ododo, and first ladies from Kogi, Kwara, Zamfara, and Cross River states, alongside leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC). With the decoration, Mrs Tinubu is only the third prominent Nigerian woman to receive the Ikele beads. item.title: Fuel scooping, recurring deaths
item.description: Many people were feared dead yesterday, while 10 others sustained varying degrees of injury when a fallen fuel tanker exploded at Oluku on the Benin-Lagos Road in Edo State. Daily Trust could not independently confirm the number of fatalities. However, some security officials, who declined to speak officially, said five people were reportedly killed in the incident. Oluku is a busy area where drivers of articulated and heavy-duty trucks often park to rest before continuing their journeys. The incident occurred near Oluku Market, destroying several shops, houses and vehicles in the area. Importation, insecurity threaten Nigeria’s food sufficiency How Senator Mandiya died in Abuja home The explosion occurred in the early hours of Thursday when a petrol tanker attempting to make a U-turn near the market fell and spilled its contents onto the road. Witnesses said that shortly after the tanker fell, residents and passers-by rushed to the scene and began scooping fuel from the road and drainage channels. One of the witnesses, who identified himself simply as John, said he had joined some people who were scooping the fuel before security operatives arrived at the scene and cordoned off the area. He said the truck owner had brought another tanker to evacuate the remaining fuel from the fallen vehicle when it exploded, leaving several victims burnt beyond recognition and many others injured. According to him, 10 injured victims were rushed to the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) for medical attention, while some corpses were deposited at the hospital’s mortuary. He said, “I was also among those scooping the fuel. I escaped by the whiskers. A soldier called me and drew my attention to the fact that the weather was hot and that the way people were rushing to scoop the fuel could ignite a fire. “As I looked back after he spoke to me, the tanker burst into flames, and people around the area scampered for safety. I thank the soldier; if not, I would have been burnt by now. “Two men who were directly under the tanker were burnt, while shops built on the drainage were also razed. We are yet to ascertain the number of people who died.” Another witness, Juliet Philip, blamed the incident on the refusal of some residents to heed warnings against scooping fuel from the fallen tanker. She said the perpetrators ignored some people, who attempted to stop them from the act, as they reportedly argued that petrol was selling for N1,500 per litre and they intended to sell what they collected. Philip explained that many people were trapped when the tanker exploded, adding that several shops at Oluku Market and vehicles parked in the area were destroyed by the inferno. “The market was seriously affected because the fuel spilled into the drainage channels within the market.
